Rare spells are offered less often.
The forge is cold, but the anvil is not. Someone was working here very recently and left in a hurry. Their tools are laid out in perfect order.
The anvil remembers the work. Your weapon comes out of the quench better than it went in. Your hands come out burnt.
You beat out the dents and fold in something new. It fits better than it did.
A great bronze bell hangs in an open arch over nothing. The wind rings it now and then, and the halls answer with movement.
The note goes through you and keeps going. Your blood runs faster. So does everything that heard.
You pry away what you can carry. The bell falls silent, and the wind with it.
A basin of black stone stands in an alcove, its lip worn smooth by kneeling. Dried runnels stain the floor beneath it. Something glints at the bottom, and something deeper still is thirsty.
The basin drinks. When it is done, it gives back what it was guarding.
Your fingers close on something cold and real.
Something closes on your fingers first.
A robed figure kneels before a brazier, feeding it with its own fingers. It has very few left. "The Crown hungers," it says. "Feed it, and it teaches."
The flame takes its due. In return it shows you three ways to burn.
The brazier swallows your Embers and spits back a spell.
A pool of molten ember seethes in a ring of black glass. Weapons have been plunged into it and abandoned, their hilts blackened, their blades gone strange.
The metal drinks the fire and keeps some for itself. So do you.
Pull a blade from the font
The hilt is very hot. You hold on.
A hunched merchant squats on a heap of coals, counting Embers that are not his. "Borrow now," he purrs, "and repay as you go."
The Embers are hot in your hand. The debt is colder.
He sells you a trinket from deep in his coat and counts your Embers twice.
A guide lies where the dark caught him, his lantern still burning in his fist. His satchel has spilled across the floor.
His grip opens easily, as if he had been waiting to hand it on.
Oil, a charm, a roll of clean bandage. He packed well.
A champion stands sealed in clear ice, her blade raised against something that never arrived. Her eyes follow you across the room.
The ice breaks like a shout. She falls into a thousand pieces. Her sword does not.
She lives for three breaths, long enough to press her hand to your chest and pass something on.
A knight in good armour turns slowly on a chain above a pit. The chain groans with every turn, loud enough to carry far down the halls.
He comes down with a crash that echoes for a long time. His gear is yours. So is everything that heard.
You work his boots free with the tip of your blade. He does not object.
Steam rises from a spring in the ice, though the water is bitter cold. Bones rest on the bottom, picked clean and very peaceful.
The cold closes your wounds and settles into your joints.
A mapmaker sits against the wall, quill still in hand, dead a week or a century. His charts are pinned beneath a purse heavy with Embers. The ink on the top sheet is still wet.
The Embers are warm. You do not look at the wet ink again.
The routes ahead unfold in his careful hand. One of them, you notice, ends at a drawing of you.
Your reflection in the tall mirror moves half a step late, and it wears your spells differently than you do. It lays one palm flat against the glass.
For a moment you stand on the wrong side of the glass. When you step back, one of your spells has changed.
Your reflection sorts through your spells like a gambler through cards.
The silver backing is worth something to someone.
The crash carries. Something answers it.
Shelves of rotting books lean into one another. Most crumble at a touch, but a few still hold their spells, pressed between the pages like dried flowers.
The old words burn bright and briefly. You sleep an hour beside them.
A tall figure in a coat of stitched parchment bows to you. Every scrap of the coat bears a name. "Give me yours," it says, "and I will keep it safe from the dark."
It writes your name on its sleeve with a careful hand. You feel lighter, and somewhat less.
It hesitates, then pays you for it anyway. A name is a name.
It knows. It bows again, and somewhere in the dark, something learns your real one.
Three skeletons crouch around an upturned shield, rattling knucklebones in a skull. They do not look up. An empty place has been left in their circle.
The bones fall your way. The skeletons do not seem to mind.
The bones fall against you. One of them tucks your Embers into its ribcage.
You win something they had been keeping a long time.
You lose. They clack approvingly at the blood.
A whole procession stands frozen in stone mid-stride, purses still at their belts. Grit trickles from the ceiling. The Worldspine is restless here.
Stone purses, stone coins, but the Embers inside are real. A falling shard opens your cheek.
The stone creeps a little way up your fingers and stays. It does not hurt. It does not leave.
Roots as thick as a man's waist have split a vault door from its hinges. Through the gap you can see gear stacked in the dark, and the roots are still growing.
The roots fight back. You win.
You come out with something, and with most of your skin.
The roots close as you pass. You tear free with nothing.
A sarcophagus lies open a finger's width. From inside comes slow, even breathing, and the faint gleam of treasure.
The breathing stops. The treasure stays.
The lid opens from the inside first.
Something nips your wrist as you draw back. You keep what you grabbed.
A door stands alone in the middle of the hall, framed by nothing. Candles burn along its threshold. Those who pass through it, the pilgrims say, come back.
The candles gutter. When they steady, you know you have one more door to walk through.
It burns without wax, and its warmth stays with you.
A pilgrim kneels in the dust, too weak to stand. His hands are cupped as if in prayer, but they are only begging. An offering bowl sits untouched at his knees.
He eats with shaking hands, then presses his palm to your chest and whispers a blessing. It settles in your bones.
He weeps over their warmth and swears the dark will repay you.
He does not resist. You will remember that he did not resist.
An obelisk of fused glass hums in the middle of a scorched circle. Every few breaths, lightning crawls up its length and something inside it lights up.
The storm passes through you and leaves something behind.
The storm passes through you and leaves nothing behind but the burn.
It bites you on the way out, but it comes.
Bell-tenders in tattered robes sing up at the storm. When they see you, they open a space in their circle and keep singing.
The song is mostly thunder. You learn the words anyway.
The dark in this room is thicker than elsewhere, and it is listening. When you speak, it answers in your own voice. "You want to leave," it says. "I can help."
It gives you exactly what you asked for. It takes exactly what it was owed.
It laughs with your laugh. The price is smaller. So is the gift.
A stone saint weeps from a single eye. The other socket holds a gem the size of a fist, glowing faintly against the dark.
The gem comes free. The light goes with it, and the dark leans closer for a while.
Her tears fall on your brow. They are warm.
Voices rise from a dry well, your own among them, saying things you have not said yet. A bucket hangs ready on its rope. Far below, black water lies very still.
It tastes of iron and cold stone. Your wounds close. The voices do not stop.
The Ember falls a long way. Something at the bottom whispers a spell back up to you.
A rope bridge spans a chasm, the wind pulling at it like a hand at a loose thread. On the far side, a corpse has left its pack.
You reach the pack before the wind reaches you.
The wind takes the bridge out from under you. You climb back the hard way.
Slow, scraped and safe. Most of the pack went over the edge before you got there.
A body lies face-down in the dust, wearing your clothes and carrying your gear, one hand outstretched toward the way you came. You do not turn it over.
Everything in its pockets is familiar. Some of it is still warm.
It takes a long time with bare hands. When you are done, you feel harder to kill.

Melee actions target adjacent or pattern-defined nearby tiles. Ranged actions require a legal range and line-of-sight path.
Area actions resolve over a tile pattern. Push and pull resolve forced movement along a legal direction until distance, blockers, or terrain stop the target.
When a draw request empties the draw pile, the discard pile reshuffles into a new draw pile.
Each reshuffle increments fatigue. Fatigue deals direct health loss that bypasses block.
Entering or striking a trap triggers damage on its tile and creates surfaces on its four cardinal neighbors. Air traps instead push adjacent characters outward.
Outcrop cards raise crag outcrops on empty floor. An outcrop blocks movement and line of sight, can be attacked like other terrain, and leaves Rubble when destroyed.

A tile is legal only when the raise keeps every floor tile connected, so an outcrop can never seal the hero, an enemy, a pickup or an exit away. A Worldspine cage is the one exception: it may seal the single tile it surrounds.

Powder kegs and Worldspines are raised the same way. A keg blocks movement but not sight; when anything destroys it, it deals its damage to its tile and each tile next to it, setting off other kegs. Your Worldspines pulse at the start of each of your turns, hitting each enemy next to one of them once.
Rockburst and Worldbreak destroy terrain to blast the enemies next to it, or the line beyond an outcrop you raised.

The Umbra hides board tiles beyond your current vision. Enemies concealed within it cannot be directly targeted, and their identities, intents, and threat previews remain hidden.
Umbra stages grow more severe deeper in the labyrinth. Radiance effects create light, extend your vision, reveal hidden enemies, or reduce the room's Umbra stage.

Until the start of your next turn, an enemy whose melee attack hits you takes the Retaliate amount. Block and Stoneskin absorb it; Chill, Freeze and Expose do not add to it.
Melee means a melee attack or any attack made from a tile next to you. Retaliate triggers once per enemy attack. Several Retaliates add their damage and Bleed; Shock and Push use the largest.
A foe defeated by Retaliate pays its normal rewards but does not refund a card play.
Your next card this turn costs that much less Time, to a minimum of 1. The card that grants Quicken never discounts itself.
Several Quickens add up. Unused Quicken ends with your turn. The Time badge shows the discount.
Your next attack on a later card this turn gains the listed bonus: extra damage, Pierce, or Chain. A bonus naming an element waits for an attack of that element.
Several bonuses add up and are spent together by that attack. Unused bonuses end with your turn.
Rite: Exhaust. Lasts for the rest of this combat.
Playing a Rite removes the card for this combat and keeps its rule active until the combat ends, like a relic. Rites never carry into the next combat.
Health paid when you play the card. Ignores Block and Stoneskin.
Deals damage through Block and Stoneskin, leaving those defenses intact.
Relics are passive run modifiers. Some trigger in combat, some change card values, and some alter rewards.
Hover relic badges in the top HUD for their current text.
Deals its displayed damage before each movement or attack action. Clears after the affected character’s next turn.
Skips the next turn and takes triple damage from attacks until thawing.
Cancels the affected character’s next non-movement action.
The next hit against the target deals additional damage equal to Expose.
Removes the displayed amount of Block, then Stoneskin, before dealing attack damage.
Jumps between enemies and Electrified tiles within the displayed distance. Each enemy is hit once per attack.
Forces the target away from the attack’s origin in one straight line for the displayed distance. It never turns or slides around anything.
When the target is off to a diagonal, it goes along the longer side by default; Rotate switches to the other side before you commit.
If a wall, crate, outcrop, character or illusion stops it early, it collides.
Forces the target toward the attack’s origin in one straight line for the displayed distance. It never turns or slides around anything.
When the target is off to a diagonal, it comes along the longer side by default; Rotate switches to the other side before you commit.
A pull that reaches its source simply stops. Anything else that stops it early makes it collide.
When forced movement is stopped by a wall, crate, outcrop, character or illusion, the target takes 2 damage for each tile it didn't move, and so does whatever it hit. Walls take nothing.
Block and Stoneskin absorb it; Chilled, Frozen and Expose don't add to it.
Removes the item card from the run after use.
Cards resolve against board coordinates. A target is legal only when the card's targeting rule, range, line of sight, occupancy, and terrain checks all pass.
Card previews show legal targets, affected tiles, and projected result values before resolution.
Undo move (Z) takes back free movement until you play a card, unless the move revealed or triggered something.
Enemies show their next attack above them: its damage and the order they act in. Red tiles will be struck before your next turn. Press I for every enemy's full plan.
Radiance reveals the Umbra through Illuminate, Vision, Truesight and Dispel Umbra.
Creates light that reveals nearby Umbra within the displayed radius. Its duration counts down on player turns.
Expands the light around you for the displayed number of turns.
Reveals enemies through the Umbra and lets you target them. Lasts for the displayed number of turns.
Reduces the room’s Umbra stage for the rest of combat.
Fast close-range predator that closes distance and opens bleed wounds.
Its intents favor short movement paths followed by melee bleed attacks.
Ranged caster with dust bolt attacks, self-defense actions, and health-draining effects.
Its intents alternate between line-of-sight damage and preservation.
Mobile ranged skirmisher with pierce and bleed attacks.
Its intents often combine repositioning with a ranged strike.
Durable front-line guard with heavy melee attacks, block gains, and close area strikes.
It can absorb damage through defenses before its health is exposed.
Fire ooze whose attacks leave Fire tiles. Slag Shell consumes nearby Fire for extra Block; killing the ooze can split it into droplets.
Each played card adds its printed time to the acting unit's turn delay.
The turn clock orders actors by current delay and previews the next turns.
Small Fire fragment spawned by a Cinder Ooze. Its attacks leave Fire tiles.
Earth controller whose attacks cover the struck tiles in Rubble and Expose targets. Shale Shell consumes nearby Rubble for additional Stoneskin.
Air-locked jailer that pulls, pushes, and restricts movement.
Its intents use forced movement and immobilize to alter reachable tiles.
Support enemy that heals and guards allies. Its guard clears elemental surfaces beneath its target.
Ice striker that creates Ice tiles and follows up with Freeze. Refract Guard clears Ice beneath the Lancer.
Storm dragon supported by up to two Lightning Wisps. Its charged bands persist between attacks.
Overload strikes around the announced charges, then fires a separate bolt. Replace charges to shrink the blast; surviving charges remain.
Lightning minion that creates Electrified tiles. Capacitor Arc inflicts Shock when conducted through Electrified.
Tharokh raises breakable spires. Their pulses reach farther during Breath. Faultline shatters surviving spires into Rubble.
Meteorfall strikes marked cells and leaves Fire. Cinder Breath also burns the ground beside that Fire.
Crownfire detonates the surviving marked Fire while Vyraketh pursues you. Replace the Fire to deny the blast, or lure the dragon into it.

The Meteorfall card marks a line of tiles the same way. The marks stay through enemy turns; at the start of your next turn, before you draw, each marked tile takes the damage (anyone standing there, including you) and becomes Fire.
Hollow Gale blasts around Vaeloryx and along its earlier Dive wake. Its body blast pushes struck actors away.
Eye of the Storm threatens a wide ring after the dragon retreats. Escape the outer edge, or enter the eye and face a weaker bite.
Each player turn begins with a finite card play capacity. Playing a card spends one play unless an effect states otherwise.
Card play effects add temporary capacity that expires at the end of the current player turn.

An area force pushes or pulls every enemy within its radius of a center: you, or a tile you choose. Each enemy moves along its own straight line away from (Push) or toward (Pull) the center, using the normal Push and Pull rules. An enemy standing on a Pull's center stays put.
Pushes resolve farthest from the center first; pulls resolve nearest first. A stopped line collides as usual: 2 damage per lost tile to the mover and to what stopped it.
Squall pushes each enemy in its cross away from the cross's center; the enemy on the center itself is pushed away from you.
Swap places with a visible one-tile enemy or one of your illusions within range and line of sight. Large enemies cannot be swapped.
Both of you arrive normally: surfaces and traps trigger for each, and you collect loot on your new tile. A swap is not a Push or Pull, so nothing collides and Anchored does not stop it.
Skate: this turn, moving onto Ice costs no movement and Ice doesn't Chill you.
Rooted: for the rest of this turn you can't Move, Blink or Swap, including your own movement.
Anchored: until your next turn, Push and Pull against you move you 0 tiles and never collide.
Fireproof: Fire doesn't damage you this turn.
Active stances appear as badges on your character.

Cleanse removes the listed statuses from you at once: Bleed, Immobilize, Chilled or Shock. Removing Immobilize or Shock frees you for the rest of this turn, and a Shock cleanse can be played while Shocked.
Removing Chilled while standing on Ice keeps you unchilled until you next enter Ice or start a turn on it.
A Petrified enemy skips its next turn. The skipped turn still costs its normal Time on the Turn Clock, so it does not come back sooner.
Petrify also gives the enemy Block, which lasts through your next turn. It is not Freeze: there is no damage multiplier and no Chill interaction. Dragons cannot be Petrified.
Each direct damaging hit breaks one Crystal Mantle layer instead of damaging health. Cheap hits can clear layers before a heavy strike.
Each remaining layer extends Shatterstorm by one tile. Break layers during its warning to shrink the danger; the burst consumes the layers that remain.
Ice beneath Iskaldra can fuel an extra layer. Remove the visible fuel before its turn to deny the bonus.

Crystal Mantle cards give you the same layers: each direct hit against you breaks one layer instead of dealing damage. Fire, Bleed, collisions, traps and health costs bypass it. Your layers last until broken or the combat ends.
Night Coil extinguishes a marked brazier before Noctyrax announces Last Eclipse. Walk or Blink onto an unlit brazier to relight it.
Light blocks Eclipse's darkness. Relight a refuge or create Light, but evade or guard against the fixed marked ground. Refuges stay lit until Night Coil.
Noctyrax replaces defeated Acolytes, up to two alive. They hide in Umbra; Light and truesight reveal them.
Shadow minion that fights beside Noctyrax and disappears when Umbra hides its tile.
Radiance and truesight reveal its position before its ranged needles and closing strikes resolve.
Earth dragon whose Worldspines reshape the arena.
Its spires pulse alongside body attacks. Break a spire to open a route before Faultline detonates the remaining field.
Fire dragon that lays marked bands of Fire. Its breath threatens a broad fan and the ground beside surviving marked Fire.
Crownfire detonates marked Fire while the dragon pursues you. Its later bite renews the marks; replacing Fire weakens the field.
Non-piercing damage is applied to Block first, then Stoneskin, then health.
Block clears before that actor’s turn-start Fire damage. Stoneskin persists and can absorb it.
Chilled and Frozen modify direct attack damage. Fire terrain damage does not gain these bonuses or trigger direct-hit riders.
Air dragon that pulls you into reach and dives along a declared route. Its Dive wake erupts again during Hollow Gale.
Its retreating storm combines a wide ring with a weaker close bite. Choose between escaping the ring and defending inside the eye.
Ice dragon protected by visible Crystal Mantle layers. Ice under its body can fuel an extra layer.
Shatterstorm follows Mantle; breaking layers shrinks its reach. Whiteout paints crossed Ice lanes that can burst again during the pursuing Talon.
Shadow dragon and final boss of the twenty-fourth depth.
Night Coil snuffs a brazier; enter its tile to relight it. Light blocks Eclipse's darkness, but evade or guard against the fixed marked ground while fighting Noctyrax and its Acolytes.
A tile can hold Rubble and one elemental surface: Fire, Ice or Electrified. Surfaces remain until consumed, replaced, removed or combat ends.
Deals 3 damage at turn start and 2 damage when entered.
Entering or starting a turn on Ice applies Chilled. Leaving Ice removes Chilled.
Lightning attacks travel through connected Electrified tiles, hitting enemies on them. Chain can also jump through individual Electrified tiles.
Frost Circuit turns a connected patch of Ice into Electrified ground. Discharge removes a connected Electrified network and strikes each enemy on or next to it once.
Walking out of Rubble costs 2 movement instead of 1. With movement remaining, the first step is always allowed.
Takes +2 damage from attacks while on Ice. An Ice attack applies Freeze and consumes the Ice beneath the target.
Consumes selected Fire tiles to damage targets on them and their four cardinal neighbors. Overlapping blasts hit each target once.
Every fourth permanent level grants one Defiance for each new run.
Lethal health loss spends one Defiance to restore 25% max health and continue the same combat.
Defiance never refills during a run. A level milestone reached mid-run adds only the newly earned charge.
Removes the displayed surface to gain the stated effect.
Moves a surface from one tile to another.

Consume: an attack that consumes a surface deals its bonus to each enemy it hits that stands on that surface, then removes the surface beneath it. An area consumes the surface on every tile of its pattern. Some attacks can only target an enemy standing on the surface. Any surface the attack leaves is placed after the consumption.
Convert: Frost Circuit turns the chosen Ice tile and all Ice connected to it into Electrified ground, then strikes and Shocks each enemy on the converted tiles.
Discharge: choose an Electrified tile. Each enemy on its connected network or next to it takes the damage once, then the network is removed.
Wards leave a surface beneath each enemy next to you. Ice placed this way Chills an enemy only when it starts a turn on or enters the Ice.

Some cards strike every enemy you can see that meets a condition: standing on Fire or Electrified ground, Chilled, or in Light. There is no target to choose, and an enemy hidden by the Umbra is never hit.
Each strike is a direct hit of the card's element, so an Ice strike Freezes a Chilled enemy. The card can be played only while at least one enemy qualifies.
